intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech by wandering the UNESCO-listed Djemaa el-Fna square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians by day, then stay for the magical transformation at dusk when food stalls fill the air with smoke and spices. Explore the labyrinthine souks of the surrounding medina, bargaining for spices, leather goods, and handwoven textiles.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp
experiences.description: Journey to the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga and embark on a sunset camel trek into the Sahara. Spend the night in a traditional Berber camp under a breathtaking canopy of stars, enjoy live Gnawa music around a campfire, sip mint tea, and wake before dawn to witness a spectacular desert sunrise over the dunes.

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a local chef in a riad kitchen for a hands-on cooking class where you learn to prepare authentic Moroccan dishes such as lamb tagine with preserved lemon, harira soup, and honey-drenched pastilla. Begin with a guided tour of the spice souks to source fresh ingredients like ras el hanout, saffron, and argan oil before cooking and dining together.

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Step back into the grandeur of Moroccan imperial history with a self-guided or locally led tour of the 19th-century Bahia Palace, adorned with intricate zellige tilework, carved cedarwood ceilings, and lush courtyards. Continue to the nearby Saadian Tombs, a hidden necropolis of the 16th-century Saadian dynasty rediscovered in 1917, featuring stunning marble and stucco craftsmanship.

experiences.name: Ksar of Aït Benhaddou & Draa Valley Drive
experiences.description: Travel through the dramatic Atlas Mountain passes to the UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) of Aït Benhaddou, a stunning example of southern Moroccan earthen clay architecture and a famous film location for Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Continue into the lush Draa Valley, dotted with ancient kasbahs, date palm oases, and Berber villages, stopping for a traditional lunch of mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) at a local auberge.
experiences.location: Aït Benhaddou & Draa Valley, Ouarzazate Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take the 19 bus or a shared petit taxi (negotiate firmly, ~50–70 MAD) to Hotel Aday in the medina. Check in, freshen up, and take a short stroll around the quiet night streets of Derb Sidi Bouloukat to get your bearings.

meals.breakfast: N/A – on flight
meals.lunch: N/A – on flight
meals.dinner: If hungry after arrival, grab a quick snack from a late-night street cart near Jemaa el-Fna square (msemen flatbread or harira soup, ~10–15 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival taxi costs low by agreeing on a price before getting in. Have small change ready. The medina streets are narrow – the hotel is a short walk from the main road. Rest well; big day tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at a local café near the hotel (mint tea, msemen, amlou almond-argan dip, ~20–30 MAD). Then walk to the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square (5-min walk) and explore the surrounding souks: Souk Semmarine (textiles), Souk des Épices (spice market), and Souk Cherratin (leather). Bargain confidently – first prices are always inflated.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bahia Palace (entrance ~70 MAD) – a stunning 19th-century riad palace with ornate Moroccan tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Afterward, walk to the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and explore the historic Lazama Synagogue (free or small donation). Stop at the El Badii Palace ruins (~70 MAD) for panoramic views from the ramparts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna as it transforms into a massive open-air food market. Eat dinner at the square's food stalls (stall numbers 1–100 area) – try grilled merguez sausages, kefta brochettes, and fresh-squeezed orange juice (~60–80 MAD total). Watch the Gnawa musicians, storytellers, and snake charmers for free entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Local café near hotel – mint tea, msemen, honey (~25 MAD)
meals.lunch: Cheap tagine or couscous at a medina restaurant on Rue Riad Zitoun el Kedim (~40–55 MAD)
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls – grilled meats, harira soup, orange juice (~70 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes. The medina is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Beware of unofficial 'guides' who approach you – politely decline. Keep your bag close in crowded souks.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior only for non-Muslims, free) – the minaret is the most iconic landmark in Marrakech. Then head to the Saadian Tombs (entrance ~70 MAD), a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis with intricate stucco and zellige tilework. Arrive early to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mellah market for local produce and dried fruits (great for cheap snacks). Then visit the Museum of Marrakech / Ben Youssef Madrasa (entrance ~70 MAD) – a breathtaking 14th-century Islamic college with a stunning central courtyard. Spend time in the surrounding northern medina souks: Souk Haddadine (blacksmiths) and Souk Chouari (woodworkers).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Café de France on Jemaa el-Fna for a rooftop mint tea with views over the square at sunset (~15 MAD). Dinner at a local workers' restaurant (restaurant populaire) in the medina – look for places with handwritten menus and locals eating inside. Try a full set menu: soup, tagine, bread, and tea (~50–60 MAD).

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby bakery – khobz bread, olive oil, coffee (~20 MAD)
meals.lunch: Snacks from Mellah market – olives, dried figs, almonds (~20–30 MAD) + cheap sandwich
meals.dinner: Local workers' restaurant near the medina – full set menu (~55 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Ben Youssef Madrasa is one of the most photogenic spots in Morocco – go mid-morning for the best light. Combined tickets for multiple sites are sometimes available at the ticket office.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (6:00–7:00 AM) on a shared CTM or Supratours bus toward Ouarzazate (~4 hours, ~80–100 MAD). Alternatively, join a budget group tour to the Sahara (2-day/1-night desert excursion from ~600–800 MAD per person including transport, camel ride, and desert camp – book through your hotel or a medina agency the night before). The route passes through the stunning Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) in the High Atlas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ouarzazate – the 'Hollywood of Africa.' Visit the Kasbah Taourirt (entrance ~20 MAD), a massive earthen fortress and UNESCO-listed site. Walk through the adjacent ksar (fortified village) and chat with locals. If on a group tour, continue driving through the Draa Valley toward Zagora or Merzouga.
day_by_day.evening: If doing the Sahara tour: arrive at the desert camp near Zagora or Erg Chebbi dunes. Mount camels for a 45-minute sunset ride into the dunes (~included in tour). Watch the sunset over the Sahara – one of the most spectacular sights in Morocco. Sleep in a traditional Berber desert camp under the stars (included in tour price).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure – bread, olive oil, tea (~20 MAD)
meals.lunch: Roadside café in the Atlas Mountains – harira soup and bread (~30–40 MAD)
meals.dinner: Berber dinner at desert camp – tagine, couscous, mint tea, live music (included in tour)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Sahara group tour 1–2 days in advance from your hotel or a reputable medina agency. Avoid touts on the street. Bring warm layers – desert nights drop to near freezing in March. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a headscarf for the dunes.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (5:30 AM) to watch the sun rise over the Sahara dunes – an unmissable, magical experience. Take a morning walk through the dunes barefoot. After breakfast at camp, begin the return journey toward Marrakech, stopping at the Draa Valley oasis towns and palmeries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Aït Benhaddou (UNESCO World Heritage ksar) on the return route – one of the most famous earthen citadels in the world, used as a filming location for Game of Thrones and Gladiator. Explore the ksar on foot (entrance ~10–20 MAD). Continue driving back through the Atlas Mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by early evening (~18:00–19:00). Rest at Hotel Aday. Light dinner in the medina – try a bowl of tanjia (Marrakchi slow-cooked lamb, ~50–60 MAD) at a local restaurant near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at desert camp – bread, jam, mint tea, eggs (included in tour)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop near Aït Benhaddou – sandwich or tagine (~35–50 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local medina restaurant near hotel – tanjia or chicken tagine with bread (~55 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Aït Benhaddou is a must-see – allow at least 1.5 hours to explore. The return drive is long (~5–6 hours total) but the scenery is spectacular. Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Ourika Valley (~30 km from Marrakech). Take a shared grand taxi from Bab Rob gate (~30–40 MAD each way) to the valley. Hike along the Ourika River through Berber villages to the Setti Fatma waterfalls (7 cascades – hike to the first is easy, ~1 hour round trip). Enjoy the lush green landscape and Atlas Mountain views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Berber family's home for an authentic argan oil cooperative demonstration (free, no obligation to buy). Return to Marrakech by mid-afternoon. Spend time in the Gueliz neighborhood (new city) – browse the Marché Central for fresh produce and local goods, and walk along Avenue Mohammed V.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the Jemaa el-Fna area. Visit the rooftop terrace of Café Argana or a similar spot for sunset views over the medina. Splurge slightly on a sit-down dinner at a mid-range medina restaurant – try pastilla (sweet pigeon pie) or a full Moroccan feast (~80–100 MAD). Browse the night souks for last-minute souvenirs: argan oil, spices, leather goods, and Berber jewelry.

meals.breakfast: Café near hotel – mint tea, msemen, honey (~25 MAD)
meals.lunch: Riverside café in Ourika Valley – fresh trout (local specialty), salad, bread (~60–70 MAD)
meals.dinner: Medina restaurant – pastilla + tagine + mint tea (~90 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Ourika Valley is beautiful in March with spring greenery. Wear sturdy shoes for the waterfall hike. Bargain hard in the night souks – prices drop significantly in the evening as vendors want to close sales.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech. Visit the Majorelle Garden (entrance ~70 MAD, or view the exterior for free) – a stunning cobalt-blue botanical garden owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Nearby is the Berber Museum (combined ticket ~150 MAD). Alternatively, skip the entrance fee and walk through the Hivernage neighborhood gardens for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the medina for any last souvenir shopping in the souks. Visit the Ensemble Artisanal (government-run craft center near Koutoubia) for fixed-price crafts – good for price comparison. Enjoy a final mint tea at a rooftop café overlooking the medina. Pack your bags and check out of Hotel Aday.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport for your departure. Take the 19 bus or negotiate a petit taxi (~50–70 MAD). Arrive at least 2.5 hours before your flight. Enjoy one last Moroccan coffee or mint tea at the airport.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at hotel or nearby café – khobz, olive oil, amlou, mint tea (~25 MAD)
meals.lunch: Street food near the souks – merguez sandwich, fresh orange juice (~30–40 MAD)
meals.dinner: Airport café or light snack before departure (~40–60 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 7 days: Accommodation (~150–200 MAD/night x 6 nights = ~1,000 MAD), Food (~150–200 MAD/day = ~1,050 MAD), Transport (~400 MAD), Entrance fees (~400 MAD), Sahara tour (~700 MAD), Souvenirs (~300 MAD). Total: ~3,850–4,200 MAD (~$380–420 USD) excluding flights. Morocco is very budget-friendly if you eat local and use shared transport.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30. Transfer from Marrakech Menara Airport to Hotel Aday in the Medina (~20–30 min by taxi, approx 100–150 MAD). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your riad-style accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival. If hungry after check-in, grab a light snack from a nearby 24-hour convenience stall near Jemaa el-Fna square (a 5-minute walk from the hotel). Rest and prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light street snack near Jemaa el-Fna if needed — try a msemen (Moroccan flatbread) or harira soup from a late-night stall (~20–30 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep taxi fare in dirhams ready before leaving the airport. Agree on a price before getting in or use a metered taxi. Hotel Aday is inside the Medina — the driver may drop you at the nearest accessible point and you may walk a short distance with luggage.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café. Then explore the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square (5-min walk) in the morning calm before the crowds arrive. Visit the Koutoubia Mosque exterior and gardens — the most important mosque in Marrakech and a stunning landmark. Stroll through the surrounding palm-lined gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive into the historic Medina souks — explore the labyrinthine markets of the Mellah (Jewish quarter), spice souk, leather souk, and lantern souk. Visit the stunning Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD), a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan architecture with ornate tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Afterward, walk to the nearby Mellah market for fresh dates and local produce.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna as it transforms into a vibrant open-air spectacle — snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and dozens of food stalls. Enjoy dinner at one of the square's famous open-air grill stalls for an authentic and lively experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Café des Épices nearby — mint tea, msemen, honey, and amlou (argan oil dip) (~40–60 MAD)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Medina restaurant — try a traditional tagine (chicken with preserved lemon or lamb with prunes) at a spot like Restaurant Chez Lamine (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls — grilled merguez sausages, kefta brochettes, snail soup, and fresh-squeezed orange juice (~60–100 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Medina streets are uneven. Bargaining is expected in the souks; start at about 40–50% of the asking price. Keep a small bag and be mindful of pickpockets in crowded areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD) — a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917, featuring intricate stucco and zellige tilework. Arrive early to beat the crowds. Afterward, explore the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD), a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now an atmospheric ruin with resident storks and panoramic views from the ramparts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Mellah (historic Jewish quarter) for a cultural walk — visit the Lazama Synagogue and the old Jewish cemetery. Then spend time at the Maison de la Photographie (entry ~50 MAD) for a fascinating collection of vintage photographs documenting Moroccan life and landscapes from the 19th and 20th centuries.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a rooftop restaurant in the Medina with views over the city. Afterward, take an evening stroll through the quieter northern souks near the Ben Youssef Mosque area.

meals.breakfast: Café Clock Marrakech or similar — Moroccan pancakes (baghrir), honey, and argan oil with mint tea (~50–70 MAD)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Derb restaurant — try pastilla (pigeon or chicken pie with almonds and cinnamon) or a hearty couscous at a neighborhood spot (~90–130 MAD)
meals.dinner: Rooftop dinner at a mid-range riad restaurant — lamb tagine with apricots or vegetable couscous, with fresh bread and salads (~150–200 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Saadian Tombs can have queues — arrive right at opening (9:00 AM). The Maison de la Photographie closes around 6 PM. March weather in Marrakech is mild and pleasant (~18–24°C), ideal for walking.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (around 7:00–8:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert — join a shared or private guided tour to Merzouga (approximately 9–10 hours drive through the Atlas Mountains). The route passes through the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m), the kasbahs of Aït Benhaddou (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), and the Draa Valley with its ancient palmeries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Aït Benhaddou (entry ~10 MAD) — a stunning fortified ksar (village) used as a filming location for Game of Thrones, Gladiator, and Lawrence of Arabia. Explore the ancient mud-brick towers and enjoy panoramic views. Continue driving through Ouarzazate and the Draa Valley, arriving in the Merzouga area by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your desert camp near Erg Chebbi dunes. Mount a camel for a sunset ride into the Sahara dunes (included in most tour packages). Watch the sun set over the golden dunes, then enjoy a traditional Berber dinner at the camp under a sky full of stars. Berber musicians will play around the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — bread, cheese, olive oil, and mint tea (~40–60 MAD)
meals.lunch: Lunch stop in Ouarzazate or a roadside restaurant along the route — tagine or sandwich (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — harira soup, tagine, couscous, Moroccan salads, and mint tea (typically included in camp package)

day_by_day.notes: Book a reputable desert tour in advance — mid-range options include a private 4x4 with driver/guide and a night in a comfortable semi-permanent desert camp with private tents and basic facilities (~1,500–2,500 MAD per person for transport + camp). Bring warm layers — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Pack sunscreen, sunglasses, and a scarf for the dunes.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise for a magical dawn over the Erg Chebbi dunes — one of the most spectacular sights in Morocco. Climb a high dune for panoramic views as the light shifts across the sand. After breakfast at camp, explore the edge of the dunes on foot or by quad bike (optional, ~200–300 MAD extra). Visit a local Berber family in a nearby village for a glimpse into traditional desert life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the return journey to Marrakech via a different scenic route — through the Ziz Valley, Todra Gorge (a dramatic 300m-high limestone canyon), and the Dades Valley (Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs). Stop at Todra Gorge for a short walk through the narrow canyon.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight stop in Boumalne Dades or Ouarzazate — check into a mid-range guesthouse or kasbah hotel. Enjoy a quiet dinner and rest after a full day of travel and desert adventure.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the desert camp — Moroccan bread, jam, honey, eggs, and mint tea (included in camp package)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near Todra Gorge — tagine or grilled meat with Moroccan salad (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the guesthouse or a local restaurant in Boumalne Dades — lamb or chicken tagine with local bread (~100–150 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Todra Gorge is most dramatic in the morning light but still beautiful in the afternoon. The road through the Dades Valley is scenic but winding — motion sickness tablets recommended if sensitive. Confirm overnight stop arrangements with your tour guide in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Morning drive back to Marrakech through the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass. Stop at a roadside Berber cooperative to see argan oil production and purchase authentic products directly from the source (no pressure to buy). Enjoy the dramatic mountain scenery and traditional Berber villages along the route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by early-to-mid afternoon. Check back into Hotel Aday and freshen up. Visit the Majorelle Garden (entry ~150 MAD) — a stunning botanical garden designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later owned by Yves Saint Laurent, featuring vivid cobalt-blue structures, exotic plants, and the YSL Museum (entry ~100 MAD extra).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Gueliz neighborhood (Marrakech's modern French-influenced district) for a change of pace — browse contemporary art galleries and boutique shops. Enjoy dinner at a stylish restaurant in Gueliz for a blend of Moroccan and international cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the guesthouse before departure — Moroccan bread, olive oil, honey, and mint tea (included or ~50 MAD)
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch stop in the Atlas Mountains — tagine or sandwich at a local café (~70–100 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Gueliz — try Al Fassia (renowned for traditional Moroccan cuisine run entirely by women) or a similar mid-range restaurant (~150–220 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden is very popular — arrive right at opening (8:00 AM) or later in the afternoon to avoid peak crowds. The garden is a 15-minute taxi ride from the Medina (~30–40 MAD). March is an excellent time to visit as the garden is in full bloom.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD), a breathtaking 14th-century Islamic college with some of the finest examples of Moroccan architectural detail: carved stucco, zellige tilework, and cedar wood screens. Explore the surrounding northern Medina neighborhood, which is less touristy and more authentic. Browse the Rahba Kedima (spice square) for last-minute souvenirs — saffron, ras el hanout spice blend, argan oil, and dried rose petals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a traditional hammam experience at a mid-range public or tourist hammam near the Medina — a quintessential Moroccan wellness ritual involving steam, black soap (beldi), and a kessa scrub (~150–300 MAD for a full treatment). Afterward, do any final souvenir shopping in the souks. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Marrakech at a rooftop restaurant or a beloved local spot. Head to the airport for your departure flight (allow at least 2–3 hours before flight time; taxi ~100–150 MAD).

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a café near the Medina — mint tea, msemen, honey, and fresh-squeezed orange juice (~40–60 MAD)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Medina restaurant — try tanjia Marrakchia (slow-cooked lamb, a Marrakech specialty) or a classic chicken tagine (~90–130 MAD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant with Medina views — a full Moroccan feast with pastilla starter, tagine main, and chebakia (honey-sesame pastry) for dessert (~180–250 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Ben Youssef Madrasa opens at 9:00 AM. Book the hammam in advance if possible, especially on weekends. Keep enough dirhams for the airport taxi and any last-minute purchases. Note that currency exchange at the airport offers poor rates — exchange any remaining dirhams before arriving. Dirhams cannot be exported, so spend or exchange before departure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Hotel Aday in the heart of the Medina (Derb Sidi Bouloukat). Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome mint tea and light snack prepared by the riad staff. Settle into your suite and rest after the journey.

meals.breakfast: On board or at airport
meals.lunch: On board or at airport
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome platter of Moroccan mezze and pastilla bites arranged by the riad — dates, olives, harissa, and warm khobz bread served in your room or private courtyard

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer in advance. Hotel Aday is a boutique riad — the narrow Medina lanes require a local guide or tuk-tuk for the final approach from the drop-off point. Keep luggage manageable for the last 100m walk through the derb (alley).

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a traditional Moroccan breakfast on the riad rooftop terrace. At 10:00, begin a private guided walking tour of the Medina — explore the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square in the morning calm before the crowds arrive, then wind through the historic souks: spice market (Rahba Kedima), leather tanneries viewpoint, and the dyers' souk. Visit the 14th-century Ben Youssef Madrasa, one of the most stunning examples of Moorish architecture in North Africa.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, visit the Bahia Palace (Palais de la Bahia) — a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan craftsmanship with ornate tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and lush gardens. Continue to the Saadian Tombs, a royal necropolis dating to the 16th century, rediscovered only in 1917. End the afternoon with a private calligraphy or zellige tile-making workshop arranged through the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll back through Djemaa el-Fna at dusk as the square transforms — snake charmers, storytellers, and food stalls ignite the night. Enjoy pre-dinner cocktails (or fresh-pressed juices) at a rooftop terrace bar overlooking the square. Dinner at a premium restaurant in the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Riad rooftop breakfast — msemen (flaky flatbread), amlou (argan oil & almond dip), fresh-squeezed orange juice, Moroccan mint tea, honey, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant (Derb Aarjan, Medina) — contemporary Moroccan cuisine with rooftop views; try the lamb pastilla and harira soup
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Foundouk (55 Souk Hal Fassi) — a beautifully restored 18th-century caravanserai serving refined Moroccan-French cuisine; reserve the mezzanine for the best ambiance

day_by_day.notes: Book Ben Youssef Madrasa tickets in advance — timed entry recommended. Private guide for the morning souk walk enhances the experience significantly and helps avoid tourist traps. Dress modestly for religious and historical sites.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Majorelle Garden — the iconic cobalt-blue botanical garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent, now home to the Berber Museum (Musée Berbère). Arrive at opening (09:00) to enjoy it before the midday crowds. Explore the YSL Memorial and the adjacent MIAM (Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech) for a fascinating intersection of fashion, art, and Moroccan culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cooking class at a premium culinary atelier in the Medina (such as La Maison Arabe Cooking School or Souk Cuisine). Learn to prepare a traditional Moroccan feast: harira soup, chicken tagine with preserved lemon and olives, couscous with seven vegetables, and bastilla au lait for dessert. This is a hands-on, immersive 3-hour experience with a local chef.
day_by_day.evening: Hammam and spa experience at a luxury hammam (such as Les Bains de Marrakech or Royal Mansour Spa if accessible). Enjoy a traditional black soap scrub (kessa), ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage. Return to the riad refreshed for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast — beghrir (semolina pancakes with honey butter), soft-boiled eggs, fresh fruit platter, and Moroccan coffee
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class — a convivial lunch with your instructor and fellow guests in a traditional Moroccan dining room
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dar Yacout (79 Sidi Ahmed Soussi) — a legendary Marrakech institution set in a stunning riad; multi-course Moroccan feast with live Gnawa music; advance reservation essential

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden tickets sell out — book online at least 48 hours ahead. The YSL Museum requires a separate ticket. Hammam sessions should be booked 24 hours in advance. Dar Yacout is one of Marrakech's most celebrated dining experiences — dress elegantly.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech at 07:00 by private luxury 4x4 vehicle for the journey to the Sahara Desert (Merzouga/Erg Chebbi). The route crosses the dramatic High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m) — stop for photos at the summit and visit the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou ksar (fortified village), a breathtaking 11th-century earthen citadel that has served as a backdrop for films including Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Private guided tour of the ksar included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley and the Valley of Roses (Vallée des Roses) — a stunning gorge lined with rose bushes, kasbahs, and palm groves. Stop at a local cooperative to learn about rose water and argan oil production. Pass through Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa') and continue toward the desert. Arrive at your luxury desert camp or kasbah hotel near Merzouga by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Mount your camel at sunset for a guided ride into the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi — the most spectacular sand sea in Morocco, with dunes reaching 150m. Watch the sunset from the top of a dune with a glass of Moroccan tea. Overnight at a premium luxury desert camp (private ensuite tent with real beds, electricity, and hot showers).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the riad before departure — packed travel breakfast if needed
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic restaurant in Aït Benhaddou village — traditional Berber tagine and fresh salads with Atlas Mountain views
meals.dinner: Dinner under the stars at the luxury desert camp — traditional Moroccan feast around a fire pit with live Berber music (guembri and bendir drums); menu includes mechoui (slow-roasted lamb), couscous, and Saharan mint tea ceremony

day_by_day.notes: The Marrakech–Merzouga drive is approximately 8–9 hours with stops — an early departure is essential. Alternatively, a scenic flight to Ouarzazate can shorten the journey (check availability). Pack a light jacket — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a scarf for the dunes.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (05:30) for a private sunrise hike to the top of the highest dune in Erg Chebbi — an unforgettable experience as the Sahara turns from deep purple to blazing gold. Return to camp for a leisurely Berber breakfast. Optional: sandboarding on the dunes or a 4x4 desert excursion to visit a nomadic Berber family in their traditional tent — share tea and learn about their way of life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the desert camp and visit the Merzouga village and the shores of Dayet Srji — a seasonal salt lake that attracts flamingos in spring (March is an excellent time). Visit a local fossil and mineral workshop — the Sahara region is world-famous for its trilobite and ammonite fossils. Begin the return journey westward, stopping at the Todra Gorge — a spectacular canyon with 300m-high rose-colored limestone walls, perfect for a scenic walk along the river.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at a luxury kasbah hotel in the Draa Valley or Skoura oasis for the night (such as Kasbah Bab Ourika or Dar Ahlam if routing allows). Enjoy a private terrace dinner overlooking a palm grove.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at the desert camp — khobz, olive oil, honey, argan amlou, hard-boiled eggs, fresh mint tea, and dates
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the camp — Moroccan sandwiches, fresh fruit, and juice enjoyed at the Todra Gorge riverside
meals.dinner: Dinner at your kasbah hotel — refined Moroccan cuisine featuring local specialties such as lamb with prunes and almonds, served in a candlelit courtyard

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise dune climb is the highlight of the Sahara experience — do not miss it. Wear closed shoes for the dune walk. The Todra Gorge is most dramatic in the late afternoon light. Confirm your kasbah hotel booking well in advance as luxury properties in the valley have limited rooms.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure at the kasbah — optional yoga session on the rooftop or a guided walk through the palmery (palm grove oasis). Depart after breakfast and continue the return journey to Marrakech via the scenic Ourika Valley route or the Tizi n'Tichka pass. Stop at a traditional Berber argan oil cooperative run by women — learn about the labor-intensive process of hand-cracking argan nuts and purchase authentic cold-pressed argan oil directly from the source.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by early afternoon. Check back into Hotel Aday. Spend the afternoon on a curated luxury shopping experience in the Medina souks with a private guide — focus on high-quality artisan goods: hand-knotted Berber rugs, silver jewelry, hand-painted ceramics, bespoke leather babouches (slippers), and pure argan oil products. Visit a reputable fixed-price artisan cooperative to avoid bargaining stress.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar with panoramic Medina views (Sky Bar at the Selman Hotel or Kabana Rooftop). Final evening in Marrakech — a special farewell dinner at one of the city's most prestigious restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Full Moroccan breakfast at the kasbah — a lavish spread of local cheeses, honey, msemen, fresh-squeezed juices, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch en route — stop at a roadside café in the Atlas foothills for a simple but authentic harira soup and Moroccan salads
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at La Mamounia's Le Marocain restaurant — the most iconic luxury dining experience in Marrakech, set in the legendary La Mamounia palace hotel; traditional Moroccan cuisine elevated to haute cuisine; full evening dress recommended

day_by_day.notes: La Mamounia's Le Marocain requires advance reservation and smart dress code. The return drive from the desert is approximately 5–6 hours — plan accordingly. The argan cooperative visit is best arranged through your hotel or guide to ensure authenticity.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — enjoy a slow breakfast on the riad rooftop. Take a peaceful early morning walk through the Medina before the souks open — the narrow alleys are magical in the quiet morning light. Visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (the mosque exterior and gardens are open to non-Muslims) — the 12th-century minaret is the architectural inspiration for the Giralda in Seville and the Hassan Tower in Rabat. Last-minute souvenir shopping or a final mint tea at a traditional café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: optional visit to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the Lazama Synagogue — a fascinating and often-overlooked layer of Marrakech's multicultural history. Check out of Hotel Aday and arrange private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport. Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech Menara Airport. Carry the memories of the Sahara, the souks, and the warmth of Moroccan hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final riad breakfast — a leisurely spread of all your Moroccan favorites: msemen, beghrir, amlou, fresh orange juice, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café des Épices (75 Rahba Lakdima, Place des Épices) — a beloved Medina institution with rooftop terrace views over the spice square; try the zaalouk, briouats, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with Hotel Aday — standard checkout is typically 12:00 but late checkout may be arranged for a premium. Keep a small amount of Moroccan dirhams for tips and last-minute purchases. Marrakech airport can be busy — arrive early. Declare any argan oil or food products at customs if returning to the EU or US.

query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March
